documents.text:
October 1, 2026


LICENSEE:     NextEra Energy Duane Arnold, LLC

FACILITIES: DUANE ARNOLD ENERGY CENTER

SUBJECT:      SUMMARY OF AUGUST 27, 2026, MEETING WITH NEXTERA ENERGY
              DUANE ARNOLD, LLC, REGARDING A PLANNED LICENSE AMENDMENT
              REQUEST TO ADOPT 10 CFR 50.69, “RISK INFORMED CATEGORIZATION
              AND TREATMENT OF STRUCTURES, SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS FOR
              NUCLEAR POWER REACTORS (EPID L-2026-LRM-0074)


On August 27, 2026, an observation meeting was held between the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) and representatives of NextEra Energy Duane Arnold, LLC (NEDA, the
licensee) via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the meeting was to discuss a proposed license
amendment request (LAR) to revise the license to allow use of the regulations at Title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 50.69, “Risk informed categorization and treatment
of structures, systems and components for nuclear power reactors,” for the Duane Arnold
Energy Center (DAEC). The meeting notice and agenda are available in the Agencywide
Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS) Accession No. ML26219A076. A copy
of NEDA’s presentation for the meeting is at ML26236A345. A list of attendees is enclosed.

The meeting began with introductions and opening remarks from the NRC staff, followed by
introductions of NEDA staff and contractor support staff. The licensee then moved into their
presentation for the meeting, which began with background on a previous NextEra LAR to adopt
10 CFR 50.69 at DAEC, which was withdrawn based on business considerations. The licensee
then discussed their plan to resume operations at the site (the required licensing actions are
under review by the NRC staff) and described the scope of the new LAR NextEra intends to
submit to adopt 10 CFR 50.69 for DAEC, specifying the processes to be used for categorization
of different structures, systems and components (SSCs):

   •   Internal events, internal flooding, internal fire risk – Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA)
       model
   •   Shutdown risk – Shutdown safety assessment process
   •   Passive component risk – Arkansas Nuclear One, Unit 2 (ANO-2) method, with a license
       condition that allows transition to the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) Enhanced
       Passive Methodology
   •   External hazards (excluding seismic risk) – Individual Plant Examination of External
       Events screening updated using the American Society of Mechanical
       Engineers/American Nuclear Society PRA Standard screening process
   •   Seismic risk – EPRI Tier 1 alternative seismic approach as described in the LAR

NextEra stated the categorization process follows Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) 00-04
guidelines, except for seismic risk evaluation. The process includes both PRA and non-PRA
evaluations, qualitative criteria, defense-in-depth assessments, and passive categorization. The
                                                 -2-


licensee stated technical adequacy of the DAEC PRA models is established by past NRC
reviews for the Surveillance Frequency Control Program (ML120110282) and for transition to
National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) NFPA 805 (ML13210A449). The planned LAR will
also request approval for using the ANO-2 approach for Control Building Chillers, with a license
condition allowing transition to the EPRI Enhanced Passive Methodology. For seismic risk, the
licensee stated they intend to follow the Tier 1 approach used at St. Lucie Plant, Unit Nos. 1 and
2 and Turkey Point Nuclear Generating, Unit Nos. 3 and 4, and that seismic risk is expected to
be a small contributor to total plant risk. NextEra explained that they intend to request to use the
ANO-2 approach solely for categorizing Control Building Chillers because the site is actively
procuring commercial grade chillers and would need to categorize the system to qualify the
chillers prior to restart of the unit. A proposed license condition would allow transition to the
EPRI Enhanced Passive Methodology for the chillers after plant-level evaluation of pressure
retention functions, and the results would supersede the ANO-2 approach. Thereafter, the ANO-
2 approach would no longer be used. The licensee closed by stating they plan to submit the
LAR in the third quarter of 2026.

The NRC staff asked the licensee several questions during and after the presentation.
Specifically:

   •   The NRC staff asked if the licensee was having difficulty obtaining control room building
       chillers that meet necessary safety related qualifications, or seismic qualifications, or
       both. The licensee replied finding chillers that met both qualifications had been difficult,
       although they believe there may be a vendor that could supply chillers that met
       requirements. NextEra stated categorizing the system under 50.69 would allow them to
       replace the chillers with more reliable components.

   •   The NRC staff asked if the control room building chillers proposed to be replaced with
       commercial grade chillers are necessary to remove the assumed heat load per technical
       specification requirements. The licensee confirmed they are the chillers necessary to
       meet technical specification requirements, and explained that previously, the chillers
       were used to cool both the control room and other areas of the building. NextEra intends
       to split the system such that the chillers are dedicated to only supply the control room
       (safety related area) and a separate system will be used for other spaces. As a follow-
       up, the NRC staff asked if the change to the system would affect the PRA model, and if
       so, would it be incorporated into the model used to support the LAR. NextEra stated they
       would evaluate and incorporate changes, if any, into the PRA model.

   •   The NRC staff asked if there was any information of relevance to the chillers in the past
       50.69 LAR for DAEC that could better inform the staff during the acceptance review
       process. NextEra stated historical information would not be relevant, since the chillers
       are planned to be replaced.

   •   The NRC staff asked NextEra to elaborate on the plan to request to use the ANO-2
       methodology for categorizing the control building chillers and then transition via license
       condition to the EPRI methodology. The licensee stated using the ANO-2 methodology
       would allow them to categorize only the specific system/components necessary to
       support use of the commercial grade chillers, which is an efficient use of the resources
       they have during the restart period. The licensee also stated they want to move to the
       EPRI methodology because it is the most recent methodology/knowledge available.
                                                 -3-


   •   The NRC staff asked how the licensee plans to categorize the active components in the
       control building chillers/system, as the ANO-2 methodology would only be for passive
       components. NextEra stated each function of the system would be split out and
       evaluated, and active functions would be assessed with NEI 00-04.

   •   The NRC staff commented that the licensee should provide some discussion in the LAR
       to support the bullet on slide 8 of the licensee’s presentation that states, “seismic risk is
       expected to be a small contributor to total plant risk consistent with EPRI Tier 1
       approach”. Section 2.2.2 of EPRI Report 3002017583 “Alternative Approaches for
       Addressing Seismic Risk in 10 CFR 50.69 Risk-Informed Categorization” identifies the
       expectation for Tier 1 sites that a low contribution of seismic risk to total plant risk
       reduces the likelihood that a unique seismic condition would cause an SSC to be
       designated as high safety significant.

   •   The NRC staff asked if sufficient information would be provided about the ANO-2
       methodology and the EPRI methodology for the staff to review both at the same time.
       The licensee stated they would provide information on both methodologies with the
       submittal.

   •   The NRC staff asked how the licensee will provide assurance that the PRA at start up
       reflects the as-built, as-operated plant considering the derecho event prior to
       decommissioning, lack of PRA maintenance program since decommissioning and
       pending plant modifications for start-up. The NRC staff proposed highlighting impacts to
       PRA from LAR dated November 20, 2025 to revise the Facility License for resumption of
       power operations at DAEC as well as impacts to PRA from plant modifications due to
       derecho event and start up activities.

   •   The NRC staff asked if closure review was performed for open peer review findings and
       self-assessment open items listed in LAR dated August 31, 2017 to adopt 10 CFR
       50.69. The licensee noted closure review was performed and the results of that review
       would be provided.

Members of the public were in attendance. No comments were provided to the NRC staff during
the meeting. At this meeting, the NRC staff made no regulatory decisions. No Public Meeting
Feedback Forms were received.

Please direct any inquiries to me at 301-415-0680, or via email at Brent.Ballard@nrc.gov.

                                              Sincerely,


                                              /RA/

                                              Brent T. Ballard, Project Manager
                                              Operating Reactor Licensing Branch 3
                                              Division of Licensing Projects 1
                                              Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation
